catalog.name: Home Assistant
catalog.description: Your house as agent tools: read every sensor and switch, and call any service — lights, heating, covers, scripts.
catalog.hint: If Home Assistant runs on the same machine as this sandbox, use http://host.docker.internal:8123 rather than localhost — the sandbox is a container. A long-lived token never expires; revoke it on the same page that created it.

steps: Open your Home Assistant profile → Security.
Scroll to Long-lived access tokens and create one; name it after this sandbox so you can revoke it separately.
Copy the token — Home Assistant shows it once — and paste it here.

catalog.name: Paperless-ngx
catalog.description: Every document you have ever scanned, searchable by the agent: find the invoice, read what it says, tag it.
catalog.hint: The API token is per user, so what the agent can see is exactly what that user can see. Full-text search hits the OCR text Paperless already extracted, so no OCR happens here.

steps: Sign in and open your user profile.
Copy the API auth token shown there.
Or, from a terminal: curl -X POST -d "username=…&password=…" https://your-instance/api/token/

catalog.name: Jellyfin
catalog.description: Your media library as a thing the agent can search and report on — what's in it, what's missing, what's been watched.
catalog.hint: An API key is server-wide and read/write. The agent uses it for queries; ask it to check what a request would change before letting it write.

steps: Add a key named after this sandbox.
Copy it and paste it here.

catalog.name: Immich
catalog.description: Your photo library, searchable in words: find the pictures from a trip, from a person, or of a thing you can only describe.
catalog.hint: The API key belongs to one user and carries that user's access. Smart search is Immich's own semantic index — it answers "the picture of the blue door" without any tagging.

steps: Account Settings → API Keys → New API Key.
Name it after this sandbox so it can be revoked on its own.
Copy the key and paste it here.
